title: Stakeholders' Feedback on Safety of Transporting Workers on Back of Lorries and Suggestions to Ban This
what_it_is: Stakeholders' Feedback on Safety of Transporting Workers on Back of Lorries and Suggestions to Ban This

sections.label: Improving road safety for workers
sections.summary: MOT prioritises road user safety, with agencies and tripartite partners reviewing worker transport on lorries and aiming to reduce the need to transport workers.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Improving the safety of all road users is a priority for the Ministry of Transport (MOT); and this requires the collective effort by all stakeholders.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Over the years, Government agencies have been working together with our tripartite partners to continually review the transportation of workers on board lorries and to put in place practical measures that can help to reduce risks and enhance safety.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: First, we aim to reduce the need to transport the workers, such as by facilitating the co-location of worker dormitories near to where they work, where feasible.

sections.label: Ban on lorry transport rejected
sections.summary: The Government says banning transportation of workers on the back of lorries is not a practical solution, especially for some contractors.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: Some have suggested that the Government should ban the transportation of workers on the back of lorries.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Transport (Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan) (for the Minister for Transport)
sentences.text: While this suggestion is well-intentioned, it is not a practical solution, especially for some contractors.

sections.label: Lorry ban infeasible due to driver shortage
sections.summary: Banning the use of lorries is not feasible due to an acute shortage of bus drivers already experienced by several sectors.

sentences.text: Banning the use of lorries is also not feasible due to the acute shortage of bus drivers, which is already experienced by the public transport, tour bus and school bus sectors.

sections.label: Measures for worker transport safety
sections.summary: Measures rolled out with tripartite partners and NGOs include rest for dual role drivers, a vehicle buddy, and mandatory rain covers, effective 1 January 2023.

sentences.text: We rolled out several measures over the past few years, together with our tripartite partners and the non-governmental organisations (NGOs).

These include requirements for dual role drivers, or workers who also have driving responsibilities, to have sufficient rest; for drivers of lorries ferrying workers to have a "vehicle buddy"; as well as for the mandatory installation of rain covers.
These measures came into force on 1 January 2023.
